source.notes: Prepared reference profiles supplied in the Member 360 design. Geographic labels are adapted to Florida. These profiles are linked to the conditions list, but remain separate from the scored analytics population and do not update clinical records. HCC mappings and coefficients have not been validated against CMS model files. Financial estimates assume $12,000 per RAF point; they are not plan payments or revenue forecasts. Submitted and accepted scores in Risk analytics retain their existing definitions.

Recapture encounter not yet completed. Flagged per RAF Audit Phase 4 High-Risk HCC Concentration testing (vascular disease is an OIG-identified high-error category).
: clinically confirmed, pending submission or acceptance; reflected in Projected RAF.
: a prior-year HCC recurring without current-year re-documentation (per RAF Audit Phase 4, Chronic Condition Persistence testing).

: a currently coded HCC whose own current-year evidence supports a higher-specificity/higher-severity code than what was submitted - distinct from recapture because the gap originates in this period's own documentation, not a prior-year lapse (per RAF Audit Phase 4, Coding Guideline Accuracy testing).

: an HCC already reflected in Current RAF whose supporting evidence is insufficient (MEAT/TAMPER not demonstrated), creating potential overpayment/clawback exposure rather than upside (per RAF Audit Phase 4, Unsupported HCC Rate testing).
Reconciliation: 1.140 + 0.240 validated = 1.380 projected. 1.140 + 0.576 total raw opportunity (excludes audit-risk) = 1.716 potential.
Planning value uses an assumed rate of $12,000 per RAF point and is not an actual plan-specific PMPM or revenue figure.
Why is HCC confidence scored this way?

For Validated, Recapture, Specificity Review and Suspect categories, confidence reflects the number and recency of corroborating sources (prior HCC, labs, medications, clinical notes) supporting MEAT (Monitor, Evaluate, Assess, Treat) or the broader TAMPER (Treatment, Assessment, Monitoring, Plan, Evaluate, Referral) documentation framework; confidence alone never confirms a diagnosis; clinician documentation and coding validation are required before inclusion in a submitted or accepted score. For Unsupported HCC / Audit-Risk items, the score instead reflects confidence that the code is
by the record under MEAT/TAMPER - a low score signals elevated audit exposure rather than a new opportunity.
Reflects completed encounters, results and current clinical state only. No appointment scheduling data is available in source systems.
